scenes.tts: A neuron listens with its dendrites and speaks through its axon. How does it keep the two apart?
scenes.visual: Title card: Cut the Axon. One neuron on a dark dish: several green dendrites, one long gold axon running off-screen.
scenes.narration: A neuron listens with its dendrites and speaks through its axon. How does it keep the two apart?

scenes.tts: Dendrites are usually several, short and branched. They receive input from other cells.
scenes.visual: The dendrites light up in green, branching and tapering; small arrows show input arriving.
scenes.narration: Dendrites are usually several, short and branched. They receive input from other cells.

scenes.tts: The axon is usually single, even in width and often very long. It carries the action potential to other cells.
scenes.visual: The gold axon lights up; a pulse travels along it and off-screen.
scenes.narration: The axon is usually single, even in width and often very long. It carries the action potential to other cells.

scenes.tts: Polarity is the word for a cell with two distinct domains, different in structure and molecules.
scenes.visual: Label on screen: polarity = two distinct domains. Dendrite side in green, axon side in gold.
scenes.narration: Polarity is the word for a cell with two distinct domains, different in structure and molecules.

scenes.tts: The difference is molecular. Dendrites carry the protein map two, receptors for neurotransmitters, and often spines.
scenes.caption: The difference is molecular. Dendrites carry the protein MAP2, receptors for neurotransmitters, and often spines.
scenes.visual: Dendrites stained green with the label MAP2; small spines bud along them.
scenes.narration: The difference is molecular. Dendrites carry the protein MAP2, receptors for neurotransmitters, and often spines.

scenes.tts: The axon carries other proteins, such as tau, and its own channels and vesicle machinery.
scenes.visual: The axon stained gold with the label tau; channel and vesicle icons along it.
scenes.narration: The axon carries other proteins, such as tau, and its own channels and vesicle machinery.

scenes.tts: A neuron must sort thousands of proteins to the right side, and keep them there for decades.
scenes.visual: Hundreds of small protein icons stream out of the cell body, sorting into green or gold branches. A clock spins: decades.
scenes.narration: A neuron must sort thousands of proteins to the right side, and keep them there for decades.

scenes.tts: Now a puzzle from a dish. Take a mature neuron, and cut its axon close to the cell body.
scenes.visual: A blade cuts the gold axon just beyond the cell body, leaving a short stump.
scenes.narration: Now a puzzle from a dish. Take a mature neuron, and cut its axon close to the cell body.

scenes.tts: Cut another neuron's axon far from the cell body. What grows out in each case?
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, the close cut; right, a second neuron cut far out along the axon. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Cut another neuron's axon far from the cell body. What grows out in each case?

scenes.tts: Cut close, and one of the dendrites can grow out as a new axon.
scenes.visual: Left panel: one green dendrite turns gold and extends rapidly.
scenes.narration: Cut close, and one of the dendrites can grow out as a new axon.

scenes.tts: Cut far, and the old axon simply regrows.
scenes.visual: Right panel: the long gold stump regrows from its cut end.
scenes.narration: Cut far, and the old axon simply regrows.

scenes.tts: So axon is not a permanent label. It is a state the cell keeps, and losing most of the axon can reset it.
scenes.visual: A rubber stamp reading AXON is crossed out. On screen: axon = a state the cell keeps.
scenes.narration: So axon is not a permanent label. It is a state the cell keeps, and losing most of the axon can reset it.

scenes.tts: That raises two questions. How is the axon won? And once won, how is it held?
scenes.visual: Two question cards: 1. How is it won? 2. How is it held?
scenes.narration: That raises two questions. How is the axon won? And once won, how is it held?

scenes.tts: Here is the map: a young neuron in a dish, as one neurite pulls ahead.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to a young stage 3 neuron, the map that every later chapter returns to.
scenes.narration: Here is the map: a young neuron in a dish, as one neurite pulls ahead.

scenes.tts: In the middle sits the cell body. Several short minor neurites grow out from it, all alike.
scenes.visual: Labels appear: cell body; minor neurites, each drawn in its own colour.
scenes.narration: In the middle sits the cell body. Several short minor neurites grow out from it, all alike.

scenes.tts: Each neurite ends in a growth cone, the motile tip of a growing neurite.
scenes.visual: Label: growth cone, at the fan-shaped tip of each neurite.
scenes.narration: Each neurite ends in a growth cone, the motile tip of a growing neurite.

scenes.tts: One has pulled ahead, and is becoming the axon. The others will become dendrites.
scenes.visual: One neurite lengthens and turns gold (label: the axon); the rest turn green (label: future dendrites).
scenes.narration: One has pulled ahead, and is becoming the axon. The others will become dendrites.

scenes.tts: The axon's first few tens of micrometres, the proximal axon, is where the initial segment will form.
scenes.visual: A bracket marks the first stretch of the gold neurite. Label: proximal axon (future initial segment).
scenes.narration: The axon's first few tens of micrometres, the proximal axon, is where the initial segment will form.

scenes.tts: The idea to carry through: an axon is won in a race, and then held.
scenes.visual: Guiding idea card: won in a race, then held.
scenes.narration: The idea to carry through: an axon is won in a race, and then held.

scenes.tts: In a useful model, positive feedback in each neurite, strong enough to compound a lead, plus competition among them, decides the race. Growth in simple proportion to length picks no winner.
scenes.visual: Card line 2: positive feedback strong enough to compound a lead, plus competition. Footnote: proportional growth alone, no winner.
scenes.narration: In a useful model, positive feedback in each neurite, strong enough to compound a lead, plus competition among them, decides the race. Growth in simple proportion to length picks no winner.

scenes.tts: Then structures in the axon help hold the win: its microtubule tracks, and a gate near its start.
scenes.visual: Card line 3: tracks and a gate help hold the win. Gold arrows along the axon and a collar at the proximal axon.
scenes.narration: Then structures in the axon help hold the win: its microtubule tracks, and a gate near its start.

scenes.tts: Loosen the hold, and the axon can lose features. Cut almost all of it away, and the race reopens.
scenes.visual: Card line 4, two panels. Left: the collar fades and the proximal axon turns patchy green, while the far axon stays gold. Right: a cut removes nearly the whole axon, and a green dendrite turns gold.
scenes.narration: Loosen the hold, and the axon can lose features. Cut almost all of it away, and the race reopens.

scenes.tts: Won, then held. But this race was seen in a dish. Next, we watch it begin.
scenes.visual: Closing card: won, then held. Next: Five Stages and a Race.
scenes.narration: Won, then held. But this race was seen in a dish. Next, we watch it begin.
